title: Once-bleached reef shows strongest recovery on record, scientists say
summary: A reef off the coast of Western Australia, devastated by the 2016 bleaching event, now shows the strongest signs of recovery on record, according to a decade-long monitoring study. Researchers attribute the rebound to a combination of cooler water years, targeted restoration work, and reduced runoff from coastal development.

sentiment.rationale: Coverage emphasizes 'strongest recovery on record', 'rebound', and quotes scientists describing the result as 'extraordinary' and 'cause for cautious optimism'. The framing is favorable while still noting fragility.

key_claims.claim: The reef shows the strongest recovery signal in the ten-year monitoring record.
Coral cover has returned to roughly 78% of pre-bleaching levels.
Cooler water years contributed materially to the recovery.
Targeted restoration work, including coral seeding, accelerated regrowth in damaged zones.
Continued recovery is contingent on limiting future bleaching events.
